class.name: Authentication
class.brief_description: Players sign in with Google, Supabase, Firebase, Auth0 or any other service. A plugin that comes with Gobu.
class.description: The Authentication plugin: it comes with Gobu, and a project that wants it adds it in [b]Project Settings > Plugins[/b] (a folder [code]plugins/authentication[/code], as any plugin); only then this class, its singleton and its settings exist. It works on every platform. Each service has its section in [b]Project Settings > Authentication[/b] (Google, Supabase, Firebase, Auth0, Custom), with what the service shares and a block per platform for each platform's own client (Desktop, Web, Android, iOS). [method sign_in_with] signs in with one in the player's browser, and the game keeps its token ([method get_token]): to call the service's API ([code]Authorization: Bearer <token>[/code]), or to join an online game, where the server checks it with this same plugin ([method check_token]).

method.name: account_of
method.description: The account a token names, [code]"<service>:<id>"[/code] ([code]"google:1102..."[/code]), by its issuer among the services of the settings; unchecked (what it says). Empty if it is of no service of the settings.

method.name: cancel_sign_in
method.description: Stops waiting for the sign-in that [method sign_in_with] started ([signal sign_in_failed] says it was cancelled).

method.name: check_token
method.description: A server: whether [param token] is a token of a service of the settings, for this game (for any platform's client), signed with the service's keys (read the first time, and again when a token comes with a key it does not have) or the secret of the [code]GOBU_AUTH_SECRET[/code] environment variable (HS256), and not expired. Then [param done] is called with the account ([code]"<service>:<id>"[/code], empty if it is not valid) and the reason. It may be called later: when the keys are read first. An online game's server uses it by itself ([b]Project Settings > Online > Login > Check: Services[/b]).

method.name: get_account
method.description: The account this game signed in with: [code]"<service>:<id>"[/code]. Empty without a session.

method.name: get_session
method.description: The service's whole answer when this game signed in ([code]refresh_token[/code], [code]expires_in[/code], the user...).

method.name: get_token
method.description: The token this game signed in with: for the service's API ([code]Authorization: Bearer <token>[/code]). Empty without a session.

method.name: is_signing_in
method.description: Whether a sign-in of [method sign_in_with] is going on.

method.name: sign_in_with
method.description: Signs in with a service in the player's browser. On a computer (OAuth 2.0 for installed apps, with PKCE): it opens the service's page, the player signs in there, and the browser comes back to an address of this computer where the game waits ([code]http://127.0.0.1:<port>/[/code]); the game trades the code it gets for the token. In a web game: the page opens in a window of its own and comes back to [code]<page>.sign_in.html[/code], which the web export writes next to the game; Google's ID token comes straight back (with a nonce), the others' code with PKCE is traded by the game; call it when the player presses a button, or the browser blocks the window. Then [signal signed_in], and the token goes to [method Online.login] when an online game asks for a login ([b]Project Settings > Online > Login > Check[/b]); or [signal sign_in_failed]. What it needs comes from the service's section in [b]Project Settings > Authentication[/b], its block of this platform first (Desktop: each platform has its own client); [param options] given in code win. [param provider]: [code]"google"[/code] (Client Id and Client Secret of a "Desktop app" OAuth client; the token is Google's ID token), [code]"supabase"[/code] (a provider of the Supabase project, in [param options]: [code]{"provider": "google"}[/code], [code]"discord"[/code], [code]"github"[/code]...; the token is Supabase's), [code]"auth0"[/code] (Domain and Client Id; its ID token), or [code]"oauth"[/code] (the Custom section: [code]authorize_url[/code], [code]token_url[/code], [code]client_id[/code], [code]client_secret[/code], [code]scope[/code]). For all: [code]port[/code] (where the game waits: 0, any free one; a fixed one for services that want the return address registered), [code]redirect_uri[/code] (the return address exactly as the service has it registered, such as [code]"http://localhost:43210"[/code]: an address of this computer with its port; the game also waits on IPv6 for [code]localhost[/code]), [code]params[/code] (more for the sign-in page, such as [code]{"prompt": "select_account"}[/code]) and [code]token[/code] (which field of the service's answer: [code]id_token[/code] when there is one, else [code]access_token[/code]). The player has 5 minutes ([method cancel_sign_in] stops it).

method.name: sign_out
method.description: Forgets this game's session (an online game's login too); then [signal signed_out].

signal.name: sign_in_failed
signal.description: [method sign_in_with] did not sign in: the player said no, the service refused it, the window was blocked or closed, it took too long, or it was cancelled.

signal.name: signed_in
signal.description: [method sign_in_with] signed in: [param token] (also [method get_token]; given to [method Online.login] already when an online game asks for a login), and [param data], the service's whole answer ([code]refresh_token[/code], [code]expires_in[/code]...).
